title: Folder with a tab
what: Exactly the locked content: the tab reads The B2B AI Standard, the sheet head reads Open for votes, then the title and the six rows, with Your part as the only orange link. The form adds only physical parts of a document folder: a back board with a raised tab and eyelet, board thickness, a front pocket lip with a thumb notch and two score lines, and two earlier drafts whose tops peek out with placeholder lines.
why: A folder is where a working file lives while people still add to it, so the Standard reads as an open, shared file rather than a finished product. The sheet is drawn half out of the pocket, ready to be read or written on, and the last row is the empty seat in that file; pointing at it pulls the page further out, as if you were taking it to fill in your part.
how: One tilted 3D rig (pointer tilt from base.js) holds the board, drafts, sheet and lip at their own depth, so the lip really sits in front of the sheet's foot; all in neutral greys with 1px hairlines, tone gradients for the board, offset edges for thickness, no shadows. On load the folder drops in, the drafts and then the sheet rise out of the pocket (translate plus a bottom clip-path so the foot stays hidden), and the rows write in with a 50ms stagger, about 1.2s in total; hover or focus on row 06 lifts the sheet 8px and draws the accent line. Reduced motion shows the final state with no transitions; under 700px the rig goes flat, the folder keeps its tab, drafts and lip, and the list stays a full-width readable column.
